GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 was a blowout quarter: revenue of $17.23B (+14.4% YoY) and EPS of $17.55 (+24.3% YoY), with operating income of $6.49B and net margin of 29.9%. The firm is the #1 global M&A advisor by deal value ($1.66T in FY25, 36.4% market share) and is benefiting from a resurgent IPO and M&A cycle — the SpaceX IPO (largest ever, $75B raise) has Goldman as lead bookrunner, generating ~$500M in underwriting fees. The AWM segment is scaling with $3.7T in assets under supervision, providing more recurring fee income. ROE has improved to 14.7% from 12% a year ago. On valuation, the stock trades at P/E of 17.65x and P/B of 2.60x, which are at the upper end of the 1-year range (P/E 13.4-18.6x, P/B 1.6-2.7x), suggesting the stock is not cheap versus its own recent history after a +31.5% quarterly rally. The stock at $1,035.64 is near all-time highs. This caps the score somewhat — the market has already rewarded the strong fundamentals. Near-term catalysts are present: the SpaceX IPO on June 12 (tomorrow) will generate significant fees and boost attention; Fed stress test results in late June could unlock further capital returns (buybacks/dividends) since stress capital buffers are frozen for 2026; and Q2 earnings on July 14 are expected to show 25.7% YoY EPS growth. Risks include elevated 10Y Treasury yields (4.45%), rising GSIB surcharges, expense pressures, and geopolitical uncertainty. The balance sheet shows total assets of $2.06T with equity of $122.8B (leverage ~16.8x), which is typical for a G-SIB. Operating cash flow was negative $31.87B in Q1, but this is normal for banks due to working capital dynamics in trading books. Overall, a solid franchise with strong near-term momentum, but valuation is stretched after the rally, warranting a moderately positive score.
